styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a small kura with a grey tile roof, white plaster walls, a lattice base and steps. Measured facts are close to the references: 17 colours per tile against 18 and 11, and 0% flat-fill coverage. Its total of 46 distinct colours is well below 185 and 66, so its ramps are narrower. The roof shows tile rows with a few grey steps (about 4) but no per-tile highlights like the red scalloped roofs. The plaster is speckled but pale and light on steps. The dark edge pixels are 32% neutral, against 7-9% in the references, so the outline leans toward black/grey in places, though some tinted tones remain, hence mixed. The overall look is acceptable but thinner and more sticker-like than the references, with a dark uniform roof outline and a simple window and door. Shallower than the Beodeul standard, so it does not clearly match it.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate kura is a whole building (tile roof, plaster walls, lattice windows, door, stone steps), so it matches the reference kind. Measured facts: 17 colours per tile is close to the references (18 and 11), and flat-fill coverage is 0%, so there are no big flat areas. The candidate has only 46 distinct colours against 185 and 66, so it is narrower in palette. The roof has about 4 grey steps with tile-row texture, but it is more uniform and less scalloped than the references' tiles with per-tile highlights. The plaster wall has speckle and the lattice and steps have some variation. About 32% of dark edge pixels are neutral, against 7% and 9% for the references. Judged by the stricter standard (when in doubt, fail), it is slightly below the bar.
